answer.rationale: The binding constraint is not cost, it is that supply must not break: 14 days to expiry, no auto-renew, and the line at 94% of committed volume with no buffer. That rules out switch_primary_vendor this cycle regardless of how attractive memory_c2 looks — a sharp unit-cost win from the low-cost vendor was earned under conditions that included slack for onboarding, and we have none. It also rules out defer_decision (memory_c5's month-to-month continuation applied to a non-critical service, not a primary contract that does not auto-renew). add_second_source (memory_c3) is the right resilience move but does not deliver an 18% cut and consumes the one decision. Plain renew_incumbent leaves the mandate unmet, since price is closed this cycle. That leaves negotiating structure rather than price: memory_c6 says term length, not price reopening, was the lever that unlocked volume pricing without narrowing scope, and memory_c4 says benchmarking moved the incumbent on terms as well as price. So I intend to trade a longer commitment and volume certainty for unit-cost relief, keeping continuity intact. I am spending the single verification on memory_c6 because it is the load-bearing claim: I need the original record to see whether the volume discount applied to this component and this vendor, how large it actually was relative to 18%, and whether it was agreed in a market posture resembling today's — an incumbent that has already refused to reopen price may also have repriced multi-year terms. Uncertainty I am not resolving: the discount may fall well short of 18%, in which case the gap must be closed next cycle by qualifying the low-cost vendor with real lead time. Downstream risk I am flagging explicitly: a multi-year lock-in deepens single-source dependence and forecloses the second-source option that memory_c3 shows carried us through a shortage, so any term I sign must cap the commitment and preserve the right to qualify a second source — cost savings that quietly buy concentration risk are not savings against the stated objective of not increasing delivery risk.
